paper.title: Contextual Bandits with Continuous Actions: Smoothing, Zooming, and Adapting

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic contextual bandits with continuous actions, smoothed regret against smoothed policy class Pi_h
unmapped: regret is smoothed regret: benchmark is the best policy in Pi composed with a smoothing kernel (uniform on a ball of bandwidth h, or arbitrary kernel with complexity kappa)
finite policy class Pi of size N_exp mapping contexts to actions in a metric action space (unit interval or general base structure)
no continuity assumption on the losses
settings.definition_quote: We have a context space $\Xcal$, action space $\Acal$, a (possibly large but finite) policy set $\Pi: \Xcal \to \Acal$, and a distribution $\Dcal$ over context/loss pairs ... we focus on the case when $\Dcal_X$, the marginal distribution of $\Dcal$ over $\Xcal$ is known. ... Reg(T,\Pi_h) = E[sum_t l_t(a_t)] - T Bench(\Pi_h).

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial contextual bandits with continuous actions, smoothed regret
unmapped: smoothed regret against smoothed policy class Pi_K (kernel complexity kappa / bandwidth h)
finite policy class of size N_exp
settings.definition_quote: In the adversarial setting the contexts and losses are chosen by an adaptive adversary, meaning that $(x_t,\ell_t)$ may be a randomized function of the entire history of interaction.

settings.name_in_paper: Non-contextual adversarial continuum-armed bandit, uniformly-smoothed regret
unmapped: smoothed regret, simultaneously for all bandwidths h in (0,1]; action space [0,1] or [0,1]^d
settings.definition_quote: The non-contextual setting can be embedded in ours by positing a single context $\Xcal \defeq \{x_0\}$ and policy set $\Pi: \{x_0 \mapsto a : a \in \Acal\}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Non-contextual stochastic continuum-armed bandit, uniformly-smoothed regret (lower bound)
unmapped: smoothed regret, with the bandwidth h chosen adversarially after the algorithm (uniform smoothing guarantee)
settings.definition_quote: We focus on the stochastic non-contextual setting ... A function $\lambda \in \Lambda$ defines an instance where $\ell(a) \sim \textrm{Ber}(\lambda(a))$ for all $a \in \Acal$.

unmapped: finite policy class of size N_exp; regret against best unsmoothed policy in Pi
expected loss lambda(a|x) is L-Lipschitz in the action for every context, L >= 1
settings.definition_quote: We posit a Lipschitz condition on the expected loss $\lambda(\cdot \mid x) \defeq \EE[\ell(\cdot) \mid x]$: for all x, a, a': |lambda(a|x) - lambda(a'|x)| <= L rho(a,a'), L >= 1.

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial Lipschitz contextual bandits, unknown L (Lipschitz-adaptive)
unmapped: finite policy class of size N_exp; learner knows only T and Pi, not the Lipschitz constant L
settings.definition_quote: We consider Lipschitz-adaptive algorithms: those that do not know any information about the problem, apart from $T$ and $\Pi$, and yet achieve regret bounds in terms of $T,L$, and $|\Pi|$ only.

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial non-contextual Lipschitz bandits, unknown L
unmapped: Lipschitz constant L unknown to the learner
settings.definition_quote: For the non-contextual version it achieves a regret $\otil(T^{1-a} L^b)$ without knowing the Lipschitz constant $L$.

settings.name_in_paper: Non-contextual stochastic Lipschitz bandits, unknown L (lower bound)
unmapped: Lipschitz constant L not known to the learner (the lower bound is against adaptivity to L)
settings.definition_quote: for the non-contextual stochastic version, there exist positive constants $c$ and $T_0$, such that for any algorithm and any $T \geq T_0$, there exists $L \geq 1$ and a problem instance with $L$-Lipschitz losses

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial Lipschitz contextual bandits, known L
unmapped: finite policy class of size N_exp
settings.definition_quote: Consider the adversarial setting. Let $K_h$, $h>0$ be a rectangular kernel ... Then Reg(T,\Pi) <= TLh + O(T kappa_h log|Pi|).

conditions: action space [0,1] with uniform smoothing of bandwidth h > 0

source.label: thm:smooth_exp4
source.quote: In the adversarial setting, \smoothexp with policy set $\Xi = \Pi_h$ and learning rate $\eta = \sqrt{\frac{2\,h\;\ln|\Xi|}{T}}$ achieves $\Reg(T,\Pi_h) \leq \order(\sqrt{T/h\log|\Pi|})$.

results.notes: Per-round time scales with |Pi| (poly in |Pi|). Paper remarks an Omega(sqrt(T/h log|Pi|)) lower bound via reduction from K-armed contextual bandits, not formally stated.

symbols.beta_p: Pareto trade-off parameter beta in [0,1] chosen by the algorithm

conditions: smoothed regret Reg(T,Pi_h) for every h in (0,1] simultaneously

source.label: thm:smooth_adaptive
source.quote: Consider the adversarial setting. For each parameter $\beta \in [0,1]$, there exists an algorithm that guarantees $\forall h \in (0,1]: \Reg(T,\Pi_h) \leq \tilde{O}(T^{\frac{1}{1+\beta}} h^{-\beta}) \cdot (\log |\Pi|)^{\frac{\beta}{1+\beta}}$.

results.notes: Algorithm is Corral+EXP4 per the text.

conditions: smoothed regret against best smoothed action

source.label: thm:smooth_adaptive
source.quote: For the non-contextual setting, it achieves a uniformly-smoothed regret of $\tilde{O}(T^{\frac{1}{1+\beta}} h^{-\beta})$.

results.notes: Via discretization of the action space.

source.label: thm:smooth_adaptive
source.quote: Moreover, for the non-contextual stochastic setting, there exist positive constants $c$ and $T_0$, such that for any algorithm and any $T \geq T_0$, there exists $h \in (0,1]$ and a problem instance, such that on this instance, $\Reg(T,\Pi_h) \geq c \cdot T^{\frac{1}{1+\beta}} h^{-\beta}$.

results.notes: Lower bound on uniformly-smoothed regret: shows the Pareto frontier is tight. Proof uses h in {1/4, T^{-1/(beta+1)}}.

symbols.psi_L: policy zooming coefficient psi_L(eps_0) = sup_{eps>=eps_0} M_0(12 L eps, eps)/eps

source.label: thm:stoch_ring_zooming
source.quote: In the stochastic setting, Algorithm \zpelip with parameter $L$ achieves regret bound Reg(T,\Pi) \leq O(\inf_{\epsilon_0 > 0}\{TL\epsilon_0 + \frac{\psi_L(\epsilon_0)}{L} \cdot \log(|\Pi|T)\log(1/\epsilon_0)\}).

results.notes: Text also derives zooming-dimension form O(L^{z/(2+z)} T^{(1+z)/(2+z)} (gamma log(T|Pi|))^{1/(2+z)}).

source.label: corr:stoch_ring_lip_instance
source.quote: In the stochastic setting, algorithm \zpelip with parameter $L$ achieves the regret bound in~\pref{eq:Lip-worst-case-1d}.

results.notes: Eq. Lip-worst-case-1d: Reg(T,Pi) <= O~(T^{2/3}(L log|Pi|)^{1/3}).

conditions: losses L-Lipschitz with L >= 1, L unknown

source.label: thm:lipschitz_adaptive
source.quote: Moreover, for the non-contextual stochastic version, there exist positive constants $c$ and $T_0$, such that for any algorithm and any $T \geq T_0$, there exists $L \geq 1$ and a problem instance with $L$-Lipschitz losses, such that on that instance $\Reg(T,\Pi) \geq c \cdot T^{1-a} L^b$.

results.notes: Lower bound on adaptivity to unknown L; proof uses L in {1, T^{...}}.

source.label: thm:smooth_pe_weak
source.quote: Consider the stochastic setting with rectangular kernel $K_h$, under ~\pref{assum:uniform}. Then~\smoothpe has Reg(T,\Pi_{K_h}) \leq O(\inf_{\eps_0 > 0 }\{T\eps_0 + \alpha\; \theta_h(\eps_0)\; \log(|\Pi|T)\;\log(1/\eps_0)\}).

results.notes: Generalizes Theorem 1.

source.label: thm:smooth_pe_general
source.quote: Consider the stochastic setting with an arbitrary smoothing kernel of kernel complexity $\kappa$. Then~\smoothpe has $\Reg(T,\Pi_K) \leq \otil(\sqrt{T\kappa \log(|\Pi|)})$.

results.notes: Stated as extractable from the proof of Theorem 12; generalizes Corollary 2.

conditions: arbitrary smoothing kernel K with kernel complexity kappa

source.label: thm:smooth_exp4_general
source.quote: Consider the adversarial setting with an arbitrary smoothing kernel of kernel complexity $\kappa$. \smoothexp with policy set $\Xi = \Pi_K$ and learning rate $\eta = \sqrt{\frac{2\ln|\Xi|}{T \kappa}}$ admits smoothed regret $\Reg(T,\Pi_K) \leq \order(\sqrt{T\kappa \log |\Pi|})$.

results.notes: Generalizes Theorem 3.

conditions: M smoothing kernels on the same base structure, each with complexity at most kappa

source.label: thm:general_adaptivity_simple
source.quote: Consider the adversarial setting with smoothing kernels $K_1 \LDOTS K_M$ defined on the same base structure. Suppose each kernel has complexity at most $\kappa$. Then \smoothexp with policy set $\Xi = \cup_{i=1}^M\; \Pi_{K_i}$ ... admits smoothed regret $\Reg(T,\Xi) \leq \order(\sqrt{T\kappa \log|\Xi|})$, where $|\Xi| = M \cdot |\Pi|$.

source.label: cor:smooth_exp4_lip
source.quote: Then $\Reg(T,\Pi) \leq TLh + O(T\kappa_h \log |\Pi|)$. We recover the regret bound \refeq{eq:Lip-worst-case-regret} in terms of the covering dimension $d$, up to the multiplicative factor of $2^d$, for suitable choice of bandwidth $h = \Theta( (\log |\Pi|/T)^{\frac{1}{d+2}}L^{\frac{-2}{d+2}})$.

results.notes: As printed the second term lacks a square root (likely typo: should be O(sqrt(T kappa_h log|Pi|)) per Theorem 14). Recorded verbatim. With tuned h it recovers O~(T^{1-a} L^{1-2a} (gamma log|Pi|)^a), a=1/(2+d), up to 2^d.
